editions.text:
The 201 feeder visits marked a slight increase over the past week's average, while the 224 acoustic detections fell below the recent mean of 288.7. The station recorded its first confident visual of a Brown-headed Cowbird. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees led visual traffic with 99 and 41 visits respectively, while Carolina Wrens remained the most frequently heard species.

The new audio source installed on September 13 explains the shift in detection patterns, as the new microphone captures a different profile of vocalizations compared to the previous system. The absence of Downy Woodpeckers and Northern House Wrens contrasts with the presence of first-time visual records like the Chimney Swift and Orchard Oriole.

A Northern Cardinal was seen just four minutes before sunset. The steady presence of Carolina Wrens, Tufted Titmice, and Blue Jays provided a consistent backdrop to the more sporadic visits from raptors and vultures.

The first confident visual of the day came from a Tufted Titmouse twelve minutes before sunrise, setting a brisk pace that continued through the early morning. By the time the light was fully up, these two species dominated the tube, with Carolina Chickadees joining the Titmice for a steady stream of confident visits. American Crows and Northern Cardinals carried the vocal load before the 08:00 hour.

The morning built significantly as the hours passed, shifting the balance from the early chickadee-titmouse pairings to a wider mix. By 09:00, the Carolina Wren took over the audio landscape with a surge of detections, while Eastern Towhees and Blue Jays added their voices to the mix. This morning is busier than the recent average, with 164 visits already logged against the usual 133.6 at this time.

A female Northern Cardinal was noted perching on the curved metal bar of the station, a distinct moment amid the constant flit of smaller birds.

The midday hours saw the Northern Cardinal assert vocal dominance, with detections peaking in the 13:00 hour while visual traffic on the feeder remained steady. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees continue to hold the seed tubes, accounting for the bulk of the 176 visits logged so far.

Weather has remained stable with a high of 27.9 C and light winds. A White-breasted Nuthatch provided the last visual sighting at 12:27, adding to the diversity of the 19 species identified today.

The Carolina Wren’s presence has been persistent through the afternoon, maintaining its position as a frequent vocalizer despite the shift in visual focus.
